findings.body:
**Unhandled rejection in `scenarioCancel` loses the verdict if the server exits early.**

`promptPromise` is created at Line 682. Nothing attaches a rejection handler until `await promptPromise` at Line 703. In between, the code waits `CANCEL_AFTER_MS` (5 s, Line 695).

Suppose the ACP child exits or crashes during that wait. `done()` (Lines 159-167) rejects every pending request. `promptPromise` then rejects with no handler. Node's default `--unhandled-rejections=throw` terminates the process. The `scenarioCancel` catch/`settle()`, `settleAndPrint()`, and verdict write never run. The script comments (Lines 148-151 and 537-539) state that child-exit rejections are recorded as evidence and never left unhandled. This path breaks that rule.

Attach a no-op handler right after the request is created. The later `await promptPromise` still throws and lands in the existing `try/catch` at Lines 702-706.

<details>
<summary>Proposed fix</summary>

```diff
       PROMPT_TIMEOUT_MS,
     );
+    // Mark as handled now; the real outcome is read at the later `await`.
+    promptPromise.catch(() => {});
     await new Promise((res) => setTimeout(res, CANCEL_AFTER_MS));
```
</details>
findings.title: Unhandled rejection in `scenarioCancel` loses the verdict if the server exits early.
